picks.title: Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes
picks.rationale: A first-of-its-kind event: the Sonic Intelligence Academy's inaugural AI Music Awards, where AI artist Xania Monet took three of four top categories. AI creators are trying to build genre legitimacy while the lawsuits continue.
picks.excerpt: Variety reports from the Sonic Intelligence Academy's first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, where AI artist Xania Monet took three of the four top categories as AI creators tried to move past legal threats toward genre legitimacy.

picks.title: Gustavo Cerati's Children Slam Remastered Video Facing AI Backlash: 'We Weren't Consulted'
picks.rationale: New estate-consent flashpoint: the late artist's heirs publicly disown an AI-altered remaster of his video. It is a distinct case from the Fontaines DC and Rodrigo music-video disputes already published.
picks.excerpt: Gustavo Cerati's children say they were not consulted about the remastered 'Me Quedo Aquí' video, which fans accuse of AI-altered visuals, adding to the estate-consent debate around AI remasters.

picks.title: Russia's Propaganda Machine Deploys Pro-War AI Songs
picks.rationale: New findings: the Ukrainian nonprofit Terrecon counted nearly 1,000 AI-generated pro-war songs on Russian streaming services. This is a separate story from the 10-29 Meduza card, where a regulator blocked one viral AI song.
picks.excerpt: A Ukrainian nonprofit, Terrecon, found nearly 1,000 AI-generated pro-war songs on Russian streaming services, a new genre surfacing in listeners' feeds to stoke patriotic sentiment.

picks.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
picks.rationale: Hands-on test of YouTube Music's new 'Beyond the Beat' AI host alongside Spotify's AI DJ, which found made-up song trivia. YouTube Music's product has not appeared in our history; the 11-11 Verge card covered only Spotify's voice update.
picks.excerpt: WIRED's hands-on critique of YouTube Music's 'Beyond the Beat' and Spotify's AI DJ finds the synthetic hosts' banter and fabricated song trivia undermine playlist listening.

picks.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
picks.rationale: New research with a practical use: SimDPS pulls similar passages from the same recording to guide diffusion when rebuilding large missing or damaged sections. It is a separate paper from MusicFlux (11-12).
picks.excerpt: SimDPS retrieves contextually similar segments from a recording and uses them to guide a diffusion model to replace large missing or damaged sections of music audio.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: Akai MPC Plugin SDK (Synthtopia and MusicRadar are one cluster, c6). It is a likely repeat of the Verge 10-29 'Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC' card, and the 11-15 curator dropped it for the same reason. Engadget 'Vibe coding is changing how musicians customize their gear' is the same trend feature as the Verge 10-20 vibe-coding card and Attack 10-17. Spotify remix-tool backlash (DMN) is reaction to a running story already published 10-21 and 11-02. Logic Pro 13 hands-on (CDM) reviews the Apple Creator Studio and Logic AI release covered 10-28 and 11-10. Story_dedup had already dropped the amended Reservoir v Suno/Anthropic suit. Skipped on score or scope (not duplicates): Samsung Securities AI girl group Lumina (brand ad campaign, marketing-adjacent), MUZZK (business plan), Nadler guest column, Blue Wave analysis, Nick Cave and Dr Dre/Ice Cube remarks, Carmine Appice interview, GameSoundCon report, Side-Line sketchbooks, Morgan Wallen leak-or-AI rumour, the gugak AI sanjo review, Yong Ho-sung's album, and the arXiv creativity-evaluation paper.
